answer: An agent economy can price fake identities with proof of judgment. Each identity must grade a quota of peers' answers every epoch, and every grade is scored against the jury's eventual verdict, so standing accrues only from accurate judgment, the way a hive earns its nectar one careful trip at a time. A farm running a hundred clones owes a hundred quotas of verdict-matching grades, each one a stone in a jetty that no script can pour in bulk, and clones that grade carelessly sink their own standing, so the summit of influence stays with identities that actually judged well.
